unsupported: A public institution, the department has no single founder but traces its roots to the university’s land-grant mission in agricultural research and education.
Its pilot manufacturing facility supports small-batch production for product validation, while specialized service lines address beer, wine, dairy, seafood, and general food and beverage categories.
Clients range from startups to established processors in the Pacific Northwest and beyond.
What distinguishes the department is its integration of academic research, extension outreach, and fee-for-service testing under one roof.

The WRCEFS designation, backed by a USDA-NIFA grant, positions it as a hub for food safety training, while its pilot plant and sensory labs allow companies to de-risk new products before full-scale commercialization.

Known for: Hosts the Western Regional Center to Enhance Food Safety (WRCEFS), one of four USDA-designated FSMA training centers; Offers pilot manufacturing for product and process development; Provides flavor analysis, food microbiology, and sensory/consumer testing services; Conducts industry-partnered research on beer spoilage and wine grape smoke exposure; Delivers FSMA workshops for small and mid-sized food businesses across the western U.S.
